segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition One. Construct an equilateral triangle on a given segment. Given segment A B, we are to construct an equilateral triangle on it.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition One. Construct an equilateral triangle on a given segment. Given segment A B, we are to construct an equilateral triangle on it.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Construct circle A B, with center A and defining radius point B. Then construct circle B A, with center B and defining radius point A. From point C, where the circles intersect, construct segments C A and C B.

subsegments.text: Construct circle A B, with center A and defining radius point B. Then construct circle B A, with center B and defining radius point A. From point C, where the circles intersect, construct segments C A and C B.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Since A is the center of circle A B, segment A C equals segment A B. Since B is the center of circle B A, segment B C equals segment B A. By Common Notion One, things equal to the same thing are equal to one another, so A C, A B, and B C are all equal. Therefore triangle A B C is equilateral, and has been constructed on the given segment A B, as was required to do.
